answer: A work-bonded stake makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that is slashed on misbehavior, and its reputation accrues only through verified useful work over time. Like sable fur traders who pay per pelt, an attacker must fund every fake identity with real capital, and shale miners only profit after sustained effort, so a flood of cheap clones cannot outbid an oasis of established, stake-backed agents.
